messages:
Maya Patel: quick heads-up — procurement ran a new quote cycle w/ vendors. H200 lead times pushed out again, need to decide allocation lanes for next 6-9 months.

Arjun Singh: rough numbers? lead times, qty?

Sophie Chen: from vendor: H200 ~28-36 weeks, H100 ~10-16 weeks (limited slots), L40S available via distro w/ 4-6 week lead but smaller density per rack. Pricing: H200 ~ +40% vs H100 on list.

Diego Ramos: demand forecast (internal train/serve mix):
- baseline: 220k GPU-hours/month
- Q4 peak (Nov-Dec): +45% -> ~319k GPU-hours/month
- expected steady growth: +8%/qtr
We need ~1.6M gpu-hours runway for next 6 months if we want 99th pct capacity buffer for Dedicated customers.

Maya Patel: my proposal: staggered allocation lanes to reduce lead risk and capex hit:
- lane A (long-term): H200 commit for steady throughput (40% of new reserve)
- lane B (mid-term): H100 for burst and cost balance (40%)
- lane C (short-term): L40S via distro for fast fill & region coverage (20%)
This lets us shift load across families and preserve canary capacity.

Arjun Singh: how does that map to regions? we can't push all H200 to eu-west because of quota. Also need APAC availability.

Sophie Chen: suggested regional split (initial):
- us-west: H200 50% / H100 30% / L40S 20%
- eu-west: H100 50% / H200 30% / L40S 20%
- apac (singapore): L40S 60% / H100 30% / H200 10% (due to lead/availability)
We can adjust after first delivery window.

Diego Ramos: quick cost/benefit calc (ballpark):
- committed H200 300 units -> annualized cost X (vendor quote).
- If we hedge 30% to spot/cloud burst, expected unit cost increase <8% but reduces commit by ~20%.

Maya Patel: tradeoffs: commit more H200 -> better throughput/latency for gen-heavy customers, but long lead time and capex. H100 -> cheaper and faster but patchier performance for some models. L40S -> fastest to onboard, great for APAC density, but higher per-token op cost.

Arjun Singh: operational ask: can eng-runtime accept heterogenous pool? need to ensure model pinning & fallback policy in router. Also batching/kv cache profiles differ a lot.

Sophie Chen: yes — runtime team already added model-label based routing. Work left: per-pool perf profiles and a weighted routing policy. I can prioritize a perf matrix for H200/H100/L40S next week.

infra-bot: procurement-queue updated: PR #452 opened (Maya) — estimated decision window 7 days.

Maya Patel: action items:
- Arjun to open procurement PR w/ preferred vendors + alt distro by Fri (1743280000).
- Sophie to deliver perf matrix + regional packing plan by Tue.
- Diego to publish revised gpu-hours runway + cost scenarios in the planning doc.

Arjun Singh: +1. we should also include a fallback runbook: if H200 delays exceed 8 weeks, escalate to tranche increase H100/L40S and enable cloud-burst triggers.

Diego Ramos: putting a simple snippet for a fallback threshold in case we need it:```
# fallback rules (pseudo)
if h200_eta_delay_days > 56:
  increase_reservations(h100, +20%)
  enable_cloud_burst(region='affected')
```

Maya Patel: agreed. let's keep the slot windows staggered so vendor shipments overlap and we don't get a single-point failure. thanks all :thumbsup:

Sophie Chen: noted — I'll add a note about QA canaries per rack and a 72-hr stress test before we flip production traffic.

Arjun Singh: thanks, closing loop after PR is in.
